title: Which forwarding methods produce explicit or transparent mode

prose.text: The mode is a property of how a flow arrives, not a setting: {{not-a-setting}}

rows: Browser with a PAC file or manual proxy
GRE or IPSec tunnel, no browser configuration

prose.text: Mode details are in [[zia.proxy-mode.explicit]] and [[zia.proxy-mode.transparent]]; the methods are in [[zia.traffic-forwarding.gre]], [[zia.traffic-forwarding.ipsec]], [[zia.traffic-forwarding.pac]], [[zia.traffic-forwarding.zcc]] and [[zia.traffic-forwarding.proxy-chaining]].

checks.do: How the specific flow arrives, since PAC traffic over a tunnel is explicit mode, before applying an explicit-only or transparent-only rule criterion.

pac-explicit.statement: A browser sent to the Service Edge by manual proxy settings or a PAC file is in explicit mode.

quotes: The user either manually configures the browser’s settings or configures the browser to use a PAC file to send traffic to a Service Edge.

tunnel-transparent.statement: Traffic directed to a Service Edge by a GRE or IPSec tunnel at the egress router, with no browser configuration, is in transparent mode.

quotes: Instead, the traffic is directed to a Service Edge through some other means, such as a GRE or IPSec tunnel configured at your organization’s egress router.

explicit-over-tunnel.statement: A tunnel can also carry explicit-mode traffic: GRE can be used in explicit proxy mode, and the SSL Inspection CONNECT User-Agent criterion applies to explicit mode forwarded by PAC or PAC over a tunnel. A tunnel therefore does not by itself make traffic transparent.

quotes: To configure GRE tunnels with the explicit proxy mode in no default route environment, use the following set of global Public Service Edge IP addresses:
This criterion applies only to SSL/TLS traffic forwarded in explicit proxy mode (PAC or PAC over tunnel)

z-tunnel-1-connect.statement: Z-Tunnel 1.0 forwards by CONNECT requests like a traditional proxy, but the SSL Inspection CONNECT User-Agent criterion does not apply to it, for lack of user agent context. No source labels it explicit or transparent.

quotes: Z-Tunnel 1.0 forwards traffic to the Zscaler cloud via CONNECT requests, much like a traditional proxy.
and not to traffic forwarded via a transparent proxy (tunnel) or Z-Tunnel 1.0 due to lack of user agent context.

not-a-setting.statement: Proxy mode is not a setting an admin turns on: it follows from how the traffic arrives (a configured browser versus a redirected flow), and one forwarding method can carry either mode.
not-a-setting.conditions: No source says there is no proxy-mode setting; it is concluded from the vendor describing each mode by how traffic is delivered.

chained-proxy-mode.title: Proxy mode of chained proxy traffic
chained-proxy-mode.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Proxy chaining is explicit mode: the upstream proxy sends CONNECT onward to the Service Edge. No captured source states it; a lab test would settle it.

z-tunnel-2-mode.title: Proxy mode of Z-Tunnel 2.0 traffic
z-tunnel-2-mode.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Z-Tunnel 2.0 is transparent: it tunnels all traffic over DTLS or TLS with no CONNECT and identifies hosts by SNI, and it carries device and user identity metadata in the tunnel header for per-user policy. No captured source states it; a lab test would settle it.
